x: As I have said the race started in perfect weather and at 3½ miles things had sorted themselves out with a leading group of 12, then Colin 14th and another group of 12 or so led by our second claim member Jack Braughton, with Eric 24th.

Walker, Jack Braughton, and Archie Bedford were among the non-starters and of those who were running only two were in full training. Half way round the first lap, Bagnall, Paterson, Short, Masters and Baulch were all between 20th and 30th in that order and Gebbett and Trower were in the next dozen.
J. Braughton, a second claim member was 6th.
Also taking part was Jack Braughton who has now become a first claim member. He will prove very valuable when he gets back to his normal form.

Several Belgravians can be found amongst the many photographs including Jack Braughton (2nd claim), Charlie Walker, John Bromley, Bill Nankeville, Peter Bagnall, Tom Morrell, Len Herbert, John Davies, Mike Shingles, Charlie Dabbs and Gerry North.

Other members of the British team had been Belgravians during the war including Doug Wilson, Rene Howell and Jack Braughton. Among the visiting teams Canada had a Belgravian as team manager but the Belgian marathon bronze medallist Etienne Gailly became one of the heroes of 1948.
